definition: The task of automatically producing source code, typically from a natural language description, partial code, or specification.
details: Code generation is one of the most impactful practical applications of large language models, powering tools like AI coding assistants that suggest, complete, or write entire functions and programs.
story: Imagine a sketch artist who starts with static and, stroke by stroke, sharpens it into a face. The result feels creative because it is memory, reshuffled at speed. Given a starting line, the machine imagines what comes next — a word, a note, a patch of a picture. The model dreams a little, then cleans up the dream. And that is Code Generation — making something new out of everything it has ever seen.
